title: Hornbill: Class 11 English core reader
subject: English
summary: Hornbill is the NCERT Class 11 core reader: prose pieces on memory, adventure, environment and education, plus poems.
points: The book mixes prose and poetry, and each chapter is examined through short and long answer questions.
Prose chapters include The Portrait of a Lady, Discovering Tut, The Ailing Planet and Silk Road.
Poems include A Photograph, The Laburnum Top and The Voice of the Rain.
For any chapter, note the theme, the narrator's tone, two or three key images and one quotable line.
The prescribed chapter list can change with edition, so check your own copy before the exam.
example: For a prose answer, state the theme in one line, give two textual details, then close with what the chapter suggests about people or society.
mistakes: Retelling the story instead of answering what the question asks.
Quoting lines without explaining what they show.

title: Snapshots: Class 11 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: Snapshots is the Class 11 supplementary reader of short stories about choices, identity and human behaviour.
points: Stories include The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse, The Address, Mother's Day, Birth and The Tale of Melon City.
Supplementary chapters are usually tested through short answers on plot, character and theme.
Track who narrates each story, because point of view shapes the meaning.
Prepare one line of personal response per story for value-based questions.
example: A question on The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse usually asks about the theme of honesty rather than the plot.
mistakes: Confusing the supplementary reader with the main reader.
Giving a moral that the story does not support with evidence.
aliases: the summer of the beautiful white horse

title: Flamingo: Class 12 English core reader
subject: English
summary: Flamingo is the NCERT Class 12 core reader, with prose on language, loss, courage and memory, and poems on time and beauty.
points: Prose chapters include The Last Lesson, Lost Spring, Deep Water, The Rattrap, Indigo and Going Places.
Poems include My Mother at Sixty-six, An Elementary School Classroom in a Slum, Keeping Quiet and A Thing of Beauty.
Each prose chapter carries a social or moral concern worth naming explicitly in answers.
Answers score when they use the text, not just a summary of events.
example: The Last Lesson links a language lesson to identity and loss under occupation, so an answer should mention both the classroom and the political setting.
mistakes: Writing the story in the first person when the question asks for analysis.
Ignoring the poet's name and the poem's central image.

title: Vistas: Class 12 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: Vistas is the Class 12 supplementary reader, with stories about truth, power and human decency.
points: Stories include The Third Level, The Tiger King, Journey to the End of the Earth, The Enemy and On the Face of It.
Questions usually focus on character motive and the story's comment on society.
Note irony where it appears, especially in satire such as The Tiger King.
Keep one example from the text ready for each theme you state.
example: The Tiger King satirises power and superstition, so an answer should show how the king's own prophecy destroys him.
mistakes: Treating satire as a straightforward adventure story.
Mixing characters between different stories in the same book.

title: Kaleidoscope: English elective
subject: English
summary: Kaleidoscope is the NCERT English elective, with sections on prose, poetry, drama and fiction.
points: The elective asks for closer reading than the core course, including narrative technique and genre.
Drama sections need attention to stagecraft, dialogue and conflict, not just plot.
Poetry answers should name form, imagery and tone before interpretation.
The elective list differs from the core readers, so check which book your school prescribes.
example: A drama answer that mentions staging and dialogue earns more than a summary of the story.
mistakes: Using core-reader chapters for an elective paper.
Reading a poem as a story with a moral.

title: First Flight: Class 10 English
subject: English
summary: First Flight is the Class 10 NCERT reader, with prose on courage, freedom and human values, and poems on nature and choice.
points: Prose chapters include A Letter to God, Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom, From the Diary of Anne Frank and The Proposal.
Poems include Dust of Snow, Fire and Ice, A Tiger in the Zoo and The Ball Poem.
Board answers reward a clear statement, textual support and a short conclusion.
Grammar and writing questions in the paper come from the same book's exercises.
example: For A Letter to God, the theme is faith and its limits, so an answer should mention Lencho's belief and the irony of the ending.
mistakes: Ignoring word limits in the board paper.
Writing a character sketch without any textual evidence.
aliases: nelson mandela long walk to freedom
from the diary of anne frank

title: Footprints Without Feet: Class 10 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: Footprints Without Feet is the Class 10 supplementary reader of short stories with a twist or a moral question.
points: Stories include A Triumph of Surgery, The Thief's Story, Footprints without Feet, The Necklace and Bholi.
Questions centre on character change and the story's message.
Many stories end with an irony that is worth naming explicitly.
Short answers should stay within two or three sentences.
example: Bholi's transformation comes from education and confidence, so an answer should connect both to the ending.
mistakes: Describing events in order instead of answering the question asked.
Missing the irony in The Necklace.

title: Beehive: Class 9 English
subject: English
summary: Beehive is the Class 9 NCERT reader, mixing prose about childhood and courage with poems on choice and nature.
points: Prose chapters include The Fun They Had, The Sound of Music, My Childhood and Kathmandu.
Poems include The Road Not Taken, Wind, Rain on the Roof and On Killing a Tree.
Answers should link a detail to a theme rather than retell the chapter.
The writing section asks for descriptive paragraphs and letters in a set format.
example: The Fun They Had contrasts mechanical schooling with human learning, which is the theme an answer should name.
mistakes: Confusing the author with the narrator.
Writing a poem answer with no mention of form or imagery.

title: Moments: Class 9 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: Moments is the Class 9 supplementary reader of stories about fear, kindness and growing up.
points: Stories include The Lost Child, The Adventures of Toto, The Happy Prince and The Last Leaf.
Questions ask about motive, theme and the significance of the ending.
Prepare one value-based response per story.
Keep answers short and evidence-based.
example: The Last Leaf turns on sacrifice, so the ending should be read through Behrman's act, not as a surprise.
mistakes: Giving a moral that the story complicates.
Retelling the plot for a three-mark question.

title: Honeycomb: Class 7 English
subject: English
summary: Honeycomb is the Class 7 NCERT reader of stories, poems and informal writing.
points: Prose includes Three Questions, A Gift of Chappals, Quality and Expert Detectives.
Poems include The Squirrel, The Rebel, Chivvy and Garden Snake.
The writing section covers diary entries, notices and short paragraphs.
Answers should quote a short phrase from the text where possible.
example: Three Questions answers its own question through the king's actions, so an answer should connect the answer to what he did.
mistakes: Answering a poem question with the story's meaning.
Writing beyond the word limit in the writing task.

title: An Alien Hand: Class 7 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: An Alien Hand is the Class 7 supplementary reader of stories about animals, courage and difference.
points: Stories include The Tiny Teacher, Bringing up Kari, Chandni and An Alien Hand.
Questions focus on character and the lesson a story carries.
Animal stories usually carry a comment on human behaviour.
Short answers should name the character and the quality shown.
example: Chandni is about the pull of freedom, which an answer should state through the goat's choice.
mistakes: Writing a full summary for a short-answer question.
Ignoring the story's title as a clue to its theme.

title: Honeydew: Class 8 English
subject: English
summary: Honeydew is the Class 8 NCERT reader, with prose on memory, environment and achievement, and poems on nature.
points: Prose includes The Best Christmas Present in the World, The Tsunami, The Summit Within and A Visit to Cambridge.
Poems include The Ant and the Cricket, Geography Lesson and The Last Bargain.
Writing tasks include letters, diary entries and short articles.
Answers should connect a detail to the chapter's idea.
example: The Summit Within links mountaineering to inner strength, which is the theme an answer should state.
mistakes: Confusing the poem's speaker with the poet.
Leaving out the required format in a letter.
aliases: the best christmas present in the world

title: It So Happened: Class 8 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: It So Happened is the Class 8 supplementary reader of fables and stories about wisdom and generosity.
points: Stories include How the Camel Got His Hump, Children at Work, The Selfish Giant and Princess September.
Fables usually carry a stated or implied moral.
Questions ask for character and message rather than plot detail.
Keep answers to the point and quote a short phrase.
example: The Selfish Giant turns on generosity, so an answer should trace the change in the giant and the garden.
mistakes: Writing the moral without any textual support.
Mixing up characters across stories in the same book.
aliases: how the camel got his hump

title: Honeysuckle: Class 6 English
subject: English
summary: Honeysuckle is the Class 6 NCERT reader of simple stories, poems and first writing tasks.
points: Prose includes Who Did Patrick's Homework, Taro's Reward, A Different Kind of School and The Banyan Tree.
Poems include The Kite, The Quarrel, Beauty and Vocation.
Writing starts with short paragraphs, messages and simple letters.
Answers should be short, complete sentences that use words from the text.
example: The Kite compares a kite in the sky to a ship on the waves, so a poem answer should name that image.
mistakes: Writing one-word answers where a sentence is asked for.
Copying a whole paragraph instead of answering.

title: A Pact with the Sun: Class 6 supplementary reader
subject: English
summary: A Pact with the Sun is the Class 6 supplementary reader of short stories with clear morals.
points: Stories include A Tale of Two Birds, The Friendly Mongoose, Tansen and A Pact with the Sun.
Each story carries one clear value, such as kindness or patience.
Questions ask what happened and what it teaches.
Answers should name the character and the value in one or two sentences.
example: The Friendly Mongoose warns against acting in anger, which an answer should state through the farmer's mistake.
mistakes: Giving a moral the story does not support.
Forgetting to mention the character by name.

title: Aaroh and Vitan: Class 11–12 Hindi core
subject: Hindi
summary: Aaroh and Vitan are the NCERT Hindi core books, with kavya and gadya sections plus a supplementary reader.
points: Aaroh has a poetry section (kavya khand) and a prose section (gadya khand); Vitan is the supplementary reader.
Poetry questions ask for bhav (meaning), ras and alankar, and the poet's message.
Prose questions ask for theme, character and the writer's viewpoint.
Chapter selections can change between editions, so confirm the list from your own book.
example: A poetry answer should name the alankar with the line that shows it, not just list the figure of speech.
mistakes: Writing the meaning of the poem without the poetic devices asked for.
Mixing Vitan stories with Aaroh chapters.
